---
title: "Adding a table-object adapter"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# A chunk's code sits under "Show code": open when it is what the page is
# about (`fold = "open"`), closed when it only supports it (`fold = "closed"`,
# the default unless the page sets another); `fold = FALSE` shows it plain,
# and so is code of three lines or fewer.
# Its results stay outside, always shown.
.fold_src <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  f <- if (is.null(options$fold)) "closed" else options$fold
  # short code -- three lines or fewer, a chunk or the part of one before
  # its next output -- is shown as it is: folded, it would hide less than
  # the fold itself takes
  if (isFALSE(f) || length(unlist(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE))) <= 3L) {
    return(.fold_src(x, options))
  }
  paste0("\n\n<details", if (identical(f, "open")) " open", ">",
         "<summary>Show code</summary>\n\n",
         .fold_src(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fold = "open")   # this page: the code is the subject
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

<p align="right">
  <a class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm" href="extending-adapters-ja.html">In Japanese</a>
</p>

rtfreporter can read tables produced by other packages — gt, gtsummary,
rtables/tern, rlistings, flextable, and huxtable — and turn them into RTF while
preserving their metadata (column labels, alignment, spanning headers, titles,
footnotes, per-cell styles).  This article shows how to teach it about **a new
table-object type**, using the existing `gt_adapter.R`, `rtables_adapter.R`,
`rlistings_adapter.R`, `flextable_adapter.R` and `huxtable_adapter.R` as
templates.

Read [Architecture & internals](architecture.html) first for the big
picture.

## The contract

An adapter has one job: convert your object into the common **kwargs
list** that [`as_rtftables()`](../reference/as_rtftables.html) consumes.
Every field except `data` is optional.

```r
list(
  data            = <data.frame>,   # REQUIRED: the rendered body (character cells are fine)
  col_header      = <chr vector | stacked spanning rows>,
  col_spec        = list(list(col = 1L, align = "left"), ...),
  col_rel_width   = <numeric vector> | column_widths_twips = <integer vector>,
  cell_styles     = <list, one element per data row, or NULL>,
  titles_block    = <chr vector | NULL>,   # becomes the page title
  footnotes_block = <chr vector | NULL>    # becomes the page footnote
)
```

`col_header`, `col_spec` and the width fields are read from this list as they
are; an argument the user passes to `as_rtftables()` wins over them.  Of the
existing adapters, only gt sets the width fields.

`as_rtftables()` does everything else (pagination, per-page `cell_styles`
slicing, replicating shared metadata, attaching titles/footnotes).  You do
**not** build the `rtftable` yourself.

## Step 1 — a detector

Add a cheap, dependency-light predicate.  Keep it side-effect free.

```r
# R/mypkg_adapter.R
.is_mypkg_tbl <- function(x) inherits(x, "mypkg_table")
# (for an S4 class use: isS4(x) && methods::is(x, "MyClass"))
```

## Step 2 — token resolution

Tokens let users opt in/out of metadata via `read_meta =`.  List your
tokens and hand them to the shared `.resolve_meta_tokens(read, allowed, label)`
(`R/as_rtftables.R`), as every existing adapter does.  It maps `FALSE` to no
tokens and `TRUE` to all of them, and stops with an error naming any unknown
token.

```r
.MYPKG_TOKENS_ALL <- c("col_header", "alignment", "titles", "footnotes")

.resolve_mypkg_tokens <- function(read) {
  .resolve_meta_tokens(read, .MYPKG_TOKENS_ALL, "mypkg")
}
```

## Step 3 — the extractor

Return the kwargs list.  Start with `.need_pkg()` (`R/need_pkg.R`), so the
package is needed only when a table of its kind is read.  If the package is
missing, `.need_pkg()` stops with an error.  If it is older than the minimum
in rtfreporter's `DESCRIPTION`, it gives a warning, once per session, and the
call goes on.

```r
.mypkg_to_rtftable_kwargs <- function(x, tokens = .MYPKG_TOKENS_ALL) {
  .need_pkg("mypkg", "Reading a mypkg table")

  out <- list()
  out$data <- mypkg::as_body_data_frame(x)          # however your package exposes the body

  if ("col_header" %in% tokens)
    out$col_header <- mypkg::column_labels(x)

  if ("alignment" %in% tokens)
    out$col_spec <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(out$data)), function(j)
      list(col = j, align = mypkg::col_align(x, j)))

  if ("titles" %in% tokens)
    out$titles_block <- mypkg::title_lines(x)

  if ("footnotes" %in% tokens)
    out$footnotes_block <- mypkg::footnote_lines(x)

  out
}
```

Tips drawn from the existing adapters:

* **Spanning headers** are a multi-row `col_header`: a list whose upper
  elements are `list(col_cell(pos = c(from, to), label = ...), ...)` and
  whose last element is the leaf-label character vector.  See
  `.extract_spanners_body()` (gt) and `.rtables_header_segments()` (rtables).
* **Per-cell styles** go in `cell_styles`: a list with one element per data
  row, each either `NULL` or a list of vectors of length `ncol` — `bold`,
  `italic`, `underline`, `indent_twips`, `color`, `align`, `border` — with
  `NA` meaning "inherit from `col_spec`" (see `cell_styles` in `?rtftable`).
  Only the gt adapter sets `cell_styles`; rtables bakes the row indentation
  into the stub text instead.
* **Footnote marks already in the text.** If your source renders marks
  inline (gt wraps a mark in a `gt_footnote_marks` span holding `<sup>N</sup>`;
  rtables writes `{N}`), convert them to
  rtfreporter's `^{N}` superscript markup **without `gsub` backreferences**
  (some locale-broken R builds drop `\\1`) — use `regmatches()` as in
  `.convert_footnote_marks()` / `.convert_rtables_marks()`.

## Step 4 — wire it in

Four places name every adapter's detector.  Add yours to each.

**1. `as_rtftables.default()` in `R/as_rtftables.R` — the list-input guard.**
Needed only if your object is a plain list (not a data frame, not S4); the
guard must not treat it as a list of items to convert one by one:

```r
if (is.list(x) && !is.data.frame(x) && !isS4(x) &&
    !.is_gt_tbl(x) && !.is_gtsummary_tbl(x) && !.is_rtables_tbl(x) &&
    !.is_flextable_tbl(x) && !.is_mypkg_tbl(x)) { ... }
```

**2. The same function — the dispatch that resolves body and metadata.**
Add a branch to the `if (.is_gt_tbl(x)) ... else if` chain:

```r
} else if (.is_mypkg_tbl(x)) {
  tokens          <- .resolve_mypkg_tokens(read_meta)
  kw              <- .mypkg_to_rtftable_kwargs(x, tokens = tokens)
  body            <- kw$data
  cell_styles     <- kw$cell_styles
  titles_block    <- kw$titles_block
  footnotes_block <- kw$footnotes_block
}
```

`col_header`, `col_spec` and the width fields are not copied: they stay in
`kw`, which is read later.  If your class is also a data frame (huxtable and
rlistings are), put the branch before the `is.data.frame(x)` branch.  The
`stop()` that ends the chain names the supported types; add yours to its
message.

**3. `as_rtftable()` in `R/as_rtftable.R`.**  It tests the object against the
same list before it calls `as_rtftables()`, and stops with "`x` must be a
gt_tbl, ..." for a type it does not know.  Add `.is_mypkg_tbl()` to that test
and to the message.  The requirements that quote the message
(`FR-TB102`, `FR-TB106` in `inst/validation/requirements.csv`) change with it.

**4. `.is_table_source()` in `R/content.R`.**  `rtf_tables(doc, x)` calls it to
decide whether `x` is a table source.  Without your detector, `x` is not
treated as a table: `.rtf_content()` falls through to its default method, which hands
`x` to `rtfplot()` as a figure and prints it.  An object whose class also
includes `data.frame` becomes a plain table instead, without the adapter's
metadata.  Calling `as_rtftables(x)` yourself works either way, so a test of
the adapter alone does not show the gap; test `rtf_tables(doc, x)` too.

## Step 5 — declare the dependency

Add `mypkg` to `Suggests:` in `DESCRIPTION`, as `mypkg (>= x.y)` when there is
a minimum.  That entry is the only place the minimum is written:
`.need_pkg()` reads it from rtfreporter's `DESCRIPTION` when it runs, so no
version number appears in R code.  Never add the package to `Imports:`, which
holds only packages that ship with R (grDevices, grid, methods, stats, utils).
The `.need_pkg()` call in Step 3 gives the error when `mypkg` is missing.

## Step 6 — tests and docs

* Add `tests/testthat/test-mypkg-adapter.R`, wrapping every test in
  `skip_if_not_installed("mypkg")`.
* A new feature comes with its requirements: each test names an FT id and
  the FR ids it checks at its head, and the FRs are added to
  `inst/validation/requirements.csv` in the same PR.  The rules are in
  "Quality assurance: requirements, tests, traceability" in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
* Document the new `read_meta` tokens (extend `?as_rtftables`), and add the
  type where the supported types are listed: `?as_rtftables`, `?as_rtftable`,
  `?rtf_tables`, `README.md` and `_pkgdown.yml`.
* Do not edit `NEWS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `Version:` in the PR.  Fill the
  *User-visible change (for NEWS)* field of the PR template; the maintainers
  write `NEWS.md` from it.
* Run `devtools::document()`, `devtools::test()`, `devtools::check()`.

## Supplying a method from your own package

The steps above are for a package that does **not** know rtfreporter: gt,
rtables and the rest never import it, so rtfreporter carries their adapters.
If you are writing a package that **depends on** rtfreporter, do not add a
branch here.  `as_rtftables()` is an S3 generic, so register a method for your
class instead, and rtfreporter never has to name it:

```{r}
# In your package's R/ (roxygen), with rtfreporter in Imports:
#' @importFrom rtfreporter as_rtftables
#' @export
as_rtftables.my_report <- function(x, ...) {
  df <- build_the_table(x)          # your own work
  rtfreporter::as_rtftables(df, ...) # a list of rtftable pages
}
```

This writes `importFrom(rtfreporter, as_rtftables)` and
`S3method(as_rtftables, my_report)` to your NAMESPACE.  The method must return
what the default returns: a list of `rtftable` pages.  `rtf_tables(doc, x)`
then accepts your object directly, converting it up front the way it converts
a `gt_tbl`.  The dependency points the right way: your package depends on
rtfreporter, and rtfreporter does not depend on yours.

## A worked reference

The rtables adapter (`R/rtables_adapter.R`) is a compact example.  It reads
multi-level spanning headers, per-column alignment, row-label indentation
(baked into the stub text), inline `{N}` -> `^{N}` mark conversion, and the
titles and footnotes — all from a single `formatters::matrix_form()` call.
The rlistings adapter reuses the same reader.  It sets no `cell_styles`; the
gt adapter is the one to read for those.
